issue.description:
Parent: the R041 umbrella (agent-friction:umbrella). Implements R041 decision 5 as specified by the spec child. Blocked by the json-documents child for the --json shape.

Problem: there is no per-issue history command. Agents invent `history`, `events` and `log` (~30 attempts) and query the events table directly with sqlite3 (~120 commands). `bead changes` is a workspace-wide cursor feed, which is the wrong tool for "what happened to this one bead".

Scope: `bead history ID [--json]` lists the issue's events in order: time, actor, kind, revision and changed fields. Help cross-references `bead changes` and `bead why`.

Acceptance:
- Lists every event for the issue in commit order, including on closed issues; --json is one array.
- Redacted content appears only as redaction markers, never the original value; a test covers a redacted note.
- A nonexistent ID exits 3.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md R042 item 5 (commit 75dc46a6; decision record beadrs-691c4fec). Operator-requested 2026-10-28. Evidence comes from a 2026-10-28 sweep of 98 bead-rs workspaces on codinghome (50,819 beads, copies deduplicated) and of transcripts from 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-28 (292,734 bead-related shell commands; regex baselines, not release claims).

Clean-room rule: amend the governing file under research/specs/ first, in its own commit, then implement only from it.

## Evidence
- 154 issues have been `in_progress` with no update for at least 7 days across 98 workspaces (2026-10-28). The oldest is hoop-46833666, untouched since 2026-08-21.
- R034 (research/specs/stale-in-progress-diagnostics-v1.md) reports such claims, read-only.
- `bead watchdog` (5 transcript uses ever) decides liveness by searching the process table for the assignee name.
- `doctor --starvation-recovery` releases stale `in_progress` claims without presenting the observed claim epoch. It runs hourly from ~/.config/systemd/user/bead-doctor.service, in SEAM. This is the failure beadrs-3be4bf40 exists to prevent.

## Scope
- **Spec:** amend stale-in-progress-diagnostics-v1.md, plus the watchdog and starvation-recovery contract text.
- Both automated release paths select candidates by R034's threshold. They release only through compare-and-reap (beadrs-3be4bf40) with the observed epoch; a conflict is a reported no-op.
- Process-table liveness is no longer a release criterion; it may remain as an advisory column.
- `--dry-run` on both paths lists candidates with epoch, age and assignee.

## Ordering
Blocked by beadrs-3be4bf40.

## Acceptance
- Concurrency test: a candidate is observed, then re-claimed under a new epoch before release; the result is no release and a reported conflict.
- A test or lint asserts that no path in `watchdog` or `doctor` calls the unconditional release service.
- On codinghome, the `--dry-run` candidate count is recorded on this bead per workspace (baseline 154 on 2026-10-28).
- Do NOT run the releasing form fleet-wide; that is the operator's step.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass on the pushed commit.
issue.title: Route watchdog and doctor --starvation-recovery stale-claim release through compare-and-reap (R042.5)

issue.description:
ADR-005 adds the doctor ready_frontier warning for open+assigned issues and explicitly records the drawback that there is no way to mark an assignment as deliberately parked, so legitimate reservations train operators to ignore the warning. Add a reservation/hold marker on an assigned open issue that the ready_frontier check treats as intentional, that survives reopen (which preserves assignee), is visible in show/list, emits an audit event, and round-trips through the checkpoint. The marker must stay advisory — it never affects eligibility beyond the existing assignment exclusion and doctor never mutates it, even under --repair — and must be distinct from manual_blocked, which blocks a bead outright rather than annotating assignment intent (so this does not overlap the beadrs-892eb8ce manual_blocked surfacing work).

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Add a first-class way to mark an assignment as intentionally held (ADR-005 acknowledged gap)

issue.description:
ADR-004's decision requires a pinned MSRV lane in bead-rs-ci (`cargo +1.85 check --all-targets`) so the declared 1.85 floor is tested on every run instead of asserted — today it is 'true by luck, not by verification' — and requires that drift between the lane's toolchain and the manifest's `rust-version` be a CI failure, not a doc nit. No open bead tracks this lane (the ADR's dependency-refresh addendum covers only the unpinned ranges). Add the lane to the bead-rs-ci WorkflowTemplate in declarative-config with the toolchain pinned to Cargo.toml's `rust-version` and a check that fails the run on divergence; record the affected declarative-config manifest path, target cluster/ArgoCD Application, and deployment commit on the bead, and verify with a green lane run before closing.

Created by: weave strand

issue.close_reason: Implemented durable monotonic claim epochs for leased and ordinary claims, surfaced them in claim/show/schema/checkpoints, preserved them through restore and merge, and validated the transition in commit d9a32b3. Omitted credentials remain accepted pending the enforcement child.
issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-8c343a7c (claim-epoch fencing umbrella). Child 1 of 5 - issuance and visibility only; enforcement lands in later children.

Problem:
Atomic claim selection prevents two simultaneous winners, but an ordinary non-leased claim gives the claimant no durable ownership credential, and leased claims expose a fencing token whose omission is tolerated by later mutations. Without a per-claim credential there is nothing for a fence to require.

Scope:
- Implement a monotonically increasing, machine-readable claim-epoch credential issued on every successful claim, for leased and non-leased claims alike. The existing lease fencing token may be evolved into this role if its renewal semantics remain safe and documented.
- Persist it durably so it survives restart, clone recovery, and checkpoint rebuild (checkpoint-visible state).
- Monotonic per issue: a later claim on the same issue always yields a strictly greater epoch, including after release, reopen, and reclaim.
- Implement the credential in `bead claim` output and in `bead show`/JSON projection (or a dedicated claim projection) so automated consumers can retain it without a second ambiguous lookup.
- Historical lease rows must never brick or collide with a later valid epoch.

Acceptance:
- A claim on a fresh issue returns a credential; the same issue released and reclaimed returns a strictly greater one.
- Leased and non-leased claim paths both carry a credential.
- The credential appears in claim output, show/JSON output, and checkpoint-visible state.
- No enforcement yet in this child: omitting the credential is still accepted by every mutation, and all existing tests keep passing.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Implement durable claim-epoch credential issuance and claim projection

issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted) specifies a third dependency kind, `verifies`, so authors can declare a check relationship, plus a structural diagnosis for inverted verification gates (a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its blocked bead). The diagnosis must be advisory — reported, never rejected at insert time, and never inferred from issue titles. No open bead covers R025. Work: extend the dependency schema and validation for the new kind, carry it through audit events and checkpoint round trips, add the inversion report to doctor/diagnostics, and add concurrency, cycle-interaction, conformance, and unknown-field round-trip tests per AGENTS.md engineering rules.
